headline: OutSystems has opened its low-code software platform to outside AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Cursor, while keeping its security and governance controls in force.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: relevant to companies using coding agents, but mostly vendor claims and customer results supplied by the company.
importance_line: Software teams at large and regulated companies can use their chosen AI coding agent inside OutSystems with company controls, but the results cited come from OutSystems itself.
summary: IT Brief Australia reports that OutSystems, a low-code software platform vendor, has made its Agent Experience product generally available, so tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Kiro can design applications inside its platform while OutSystems generates the code and applies its security, testing and deployment rules. The company points to survey data saying 74% of AI-generated code needs major rework or never reaches production, and its customer examples, such as a law firm building a tracker in under three hours, are OutSystems' own account.
notes: Pool link (Techzine) blocked with 403; IT Brief Australia read instead; SMBtech has the same story.
